claims.text: High-temperature oxidation induces significant elemental redistribution within nanoprecipitates in additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3.
Oxidation produces enrichment or depletion of Al, Ti, and Cr at precipitate interfaces.
Al and Cr are oxidation-active elements in this class of HEAs.
The additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy contains dual nanoscale precipitates in a relatively homogeneous matrix.
The range 850–1050 °C is suitable for investigating high-temperature oxidation in an Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni-based HEA.
The proposed oxidation conditions simulate high-temperature service environments such as gas turbines or power plants.
APT provides near-atomic-resolution analysis of the oxidized microstructure.
Nanoprecipitates act as sites for elemental segregation and redistribution during oxidation.
High-temperature exposure drives diffusion that selectively migrates Al and Cr within nanoprecipitates.
APT can resolve the resulting local nanoprecipitate compositions in three dimensions.
Oxidized samples will exhibit measurable compositional gradients within and around nanoprecipitates.
Oxidized samples will exhibit phase separation within or around nanoprecipitates.
Nanoscale elemental redistribution contributes to the alloy's oxidation behavior.
Nanoprecipitates in unoxidized additively manufactured or conventionally processed cast/wrought samples have uniform elemental distributions.
The extent and nature of redistribution depend on oxidation temperature, exposure time, and external stress.
Ex situ APT provides snapshots rather than real-time observation of elemental redistribution.
APT specimen preparation may introduce artifacts affecting inferred elemental redistribution.
